articles.title: Devotees worried over conduct of Kandasashti festival at Kandakottam temple
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Govt Schemes
fullParagraphs: Devotees of the Sri Muthukumaraswamy Temple, popularly known as Kandhakottam in Rattan Bazaar in Park Town, are worried about the conduct of the Kandasashthi festival this year.

"Usually, tickets for the Laksharcharnai during the annual festival are sold just after Vijayadasami. Till date, the administration has not started selling tickets. Every year around 35,000 tickets each priced at ₹300 are sold to devotees who want to participate in the archanai that is slated to start on November 10. There is no sign of the conduct of the festival so far," said A. B. Srinivasan, a 65-year-old devotee.

Saravanan, another devotee, said that this year would be the 99 th consecutive year of the Kandasashthi festival during which grand concerts would be held. "Participants of the archanai would be given prasadam including a bucket. Tenders for procuring various items such as pandals, coconuts, bags, and flowers are yet to be called for. We hear that the executive officer has gone on leave and another person has taken charge," he said.

The over 500-year-old shrine, is a scheme temple, meaning it belongs to a particular community - in this case, the Berri Chettis. A five-member team was chosen from the community as trustees last year and they have also been in charge of the daily running of the temple.

Sendilvellan, one of the trustees, said that the executive officer had taken away cheque signatory powers from the trustees and the trustees were unable to pay salaries even. "He has gone to the bank and taken signatory powers without informing us. We seem to have absolutely no powers in the day-to-day running of the temple. The court had directed the Hindu Religious and Charitable Endowments department to interfere only if there was any problem relating to the conduct of the temple. From last year, we have been managing the temple without any problems," he said.

Another trustee said that with just a few days left for the festival they have been running from pillar to post trying to get the powers back and conduct it. Sources in the HR&CE Department said they will look into the matter.

articles.title: Rajasthan IPS officer removed after ACB probe ordered against IAS husband
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Govt Schemes
fullParagraphs: The Rajasthan government on Saturday placed an Indian Police Service (IPS) officer, Prashakha Mathur, on awaiting posting order (APO) after an investigation by the Anti-Corruption Bureau (ACB) was approved against her husband and senior Indian Administrative Service (IAS) officer Shikhar Agrawal.

Mr. Agrawal, who was also sent on APO earlier this week, is facing charges along with his family members of purchasing 40 villas in luxury resorts operated by a private firm in Udaipur and Alwar districts by allegedly abusing his position and influence and extending “undue benefits” to the firm.

While Mr. Agrawal was serving as the Additional Chief Secretary (Industries) and additionally held charge of four public sector corporations, his wife Ms. Mathur, a 1995-batch IPS officer, was posted as Additional Director General in charge of Planning, Modernisation and Welfare.

The ACB has alleged that Mr. Agrawal gave benefits such as relaxations in resort construction conditions, approvals without verification of certificates and special concessional packages to the firm. The alleged purchases of villas were made in the names of Mr. Agrawal and Ms. Mathur, their two sons, and Mr. Agrawal’s parents-in-law.

The ACB has registered a Preliminary Enquiry (PE) and launched an investigation into the allegations of abuse of official position, conflict of interest, and extending undue benefits to the firm in question.

ACB Director General Govind Gupta said the properties were allegedly purchased at prices substantially below their market value. The ACB’s probe will examine whether the alleged benefits caused substantial financial losses to the State government and whether Mr. Agrawal and his family members acquired assets disproportionate to their known sources of income.

Mr. Agrawal was appointed Additional Chief Secretary in the Chief Minister’s Office in February 2024, shortly after Bhajan Lal Sharma took oath as the CM, and served in that position till November 2025. Former CM Ashok Gehlot has demanded investigation by Central agencies into the matter, describing it as the “biggest scandal” under the Bharatiya Janata Party government.

articles.title: At CEC’s ‘public impeachment’, voters question deletion of names from rolls
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Govt Schemes
fullParagraphs: The Indian National Developmental, Inclusive Alliance’s symbolic “public impeachment” of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar on Saturday (October 31, 2026) featured accounts from voters who alleged that their names had been deleted from electoral rolls during the special intensive revision (SIR) exercise.
Among them was Anita Jaiswal, who moved from Kolkata to Delhi. She said she had voted in every election between 2012 and 2025 but was now being asked to establish her citizenship.
ALSO WATCH Watch: INDIA bloc leaders present united front against CEC Gyanesh Kumar, holds mock impeachment

“I am a single mother. They told me to get an Aadhaar card, saying it would prove that I am a citizen. Who gave you the right to remove my voter ID? My daughter gets a scholarship, has a bank account and an Aadhaar card, and now you are deleting our names. Who gave you the right?” she asked, adding, “Prove which country I am from.”

Iftikar Ahmed, another voter from Kolkata, said he had voted in the same Chowrangee constituency for 20 years but received a notice during the SIR hearing seeking documents because of a mapping discrepancy. His father, too, had been voting from the same address for two decades, he said. “Our names have been removed in a planned manner,” he alleged.

Nikhil Dey, founder of Mazdoor Kisan Shakti Sangathan, who has been working with affected voters, introduced Kanta Prasad, who had been declared dead in the exercise. “He spoke very convincingly for a corpse! The deprivation of the right to vote is a crime against the Constitution and a blot on our democracy. There must be accountability,” Congress MP Shashi Tharoor said in a post on X.
ALSO WATCH Rahul Gandhi: Deletion of 1 in 7 voters makes 2024 election ‘illegitimate’ | INDIA bloc

RTI activist Anjali Bharadwaj said that in response to an application seeking copies of files recording the decision-making process behind the SIR, the Election Commission of India (ECI) had replied that no such file existed.
“T.C. Kom, who is a Principal Secretary, said the ECI had not taken any decision to conduct an SIR,” Ms. Bharadwaj claimed.
Swaraj Abhiyan chief Yogendra Yadav described Mr. Kumar as the “Mukhya Chunav Abhiyukt (Chief Election Culprit)” rather than the “Mukhya Chunav Ayukt (Chief Election Commissioner)”.

All India Students’ Association (AISA) national president Neha Bora alleged that the SIR was a deliberate attempt to disenfranchise young voters and undermine democracy. Questioning the functioning of electoral registration officers (EROs), she said their statutory authority was being overridden through the use of software to exclude eligible voters. “You have abused your public office and favoured one political party,” she alleged.

The programme was held in the garden of Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge’s residence in New Delhi. Former Lok Sabha Speaker Meira Kumar presided over the proceedings, while Mr. Kharge moved the motion.

articles.title: Two persons held for possession of country-made guns, explosives
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Govt Schemes
fullParagraphs: Two persons, including a farmer, were arrested for possession of two country made guns and crude bombs near Pallikonda and Pernambut towns in Vellore on Saturday.
Forest officials identified the arrested persons as U. Chandru, 21, a tribal from Irular community, and G. Srinivasan, 39, a farmer.

Initial inquiry revealed that Srinivasan has been cultivating paddy and groundnuts on his two acre farmland. Forest officials said that, based on a tip-off, a special team conducted searches at his house and farmland, and found country made guns, explosives, nets, torchlights, and batteries.
Forest officials said that Srinivasan procured guns from his contacts in Kerala. He used pellets to hunt monkeys, rabbits, and spotted deer in forests surrounding Jawadhu Hills.

In a separate incident, forest officials arrested Chandru, who was allegedly loitering with a country-made gun in the area. The team nabbed him during a regular patrol and seized the country-made gun, pellets, and explosives.
Forest officials said both arrested persons were lodged at Central Prison in Vellore. Further probe is under way.

articles.title: New bridge to be opened near Sholinghur to replace British-era structure
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Govt Schemes
fullParagraphs: A new ₹3.85 crore high-level bridge across the Rendadi Water Supply Channel near Ponnai River, at Sekkadikuppam village near Sholinghur town in Ranipet will be opened for public use by December this year.

Officials of the District Rural Development Agency (DRDA), which executes the work, said that the new facility was a long-standing demand of at least eight surrounding farming villages across the water channel. The new bridge will replace the British-era causeway, which was damaged during 2021 floods in the water channel, fed by Ponnai river.

The new bridge will provide easy access to villagers in Ranipet and Thiruvallur districts. “The new bridge will help farmers to transport farm products to common markets in surrounding big towns. Buses will also be operated to reach remote villages,” S. Kannan, Assistant Engineer (AE), DRDA (Sholinghur), told The Hindu.

On Saturday, Collector N. Priya Ravichandran inspected the under-construction bridge in the presence of S. Selvarani, Project Director (PD), DRDA (Ranipet), and Prabhakaran, Executive Engineer (EE), DRDA (Ranipet). “During monsoon, residents could not cross the water channel due to chest-deep water. The new bridge will be a lifeline for residents as ambulances and government buses can reach remote villages in the region,” said T. Perumal, a farmer.

DRDA officials said that the new bridge will replace the dilapidated causeway, which was demolished for the work, to connect surrounding villages with towns like Sholinghur, Arakkonam, Tiruvallur, and Tiruttani.

Funded under the State Special Assistance Scheme for 2025-26, the new bridge will be 38 metres long and 7.5 metres wide. It can discharge around 30,000 cusecs of water per second. The new facility has been built at least three metres above the water channel to prevent inundation during floods.

The new bridge will have tiled footpaths, LED lights, inlets to discharge rainwater into the river, reflectors, signboards and hand railings. Approach roads will also be laid to connect surrounding villages with the new facility.

For residents, the new bridges will end a detour of at least eight kms to reach the nearest towns in Ranipet and Thiruvallur districts. It will provide easy access to basic facilities like government schools, health centres, banks, ATMs, agricultural office, cooperative society and taluk office, residents said.

articles.title: Two arrested for attempting to determine sex of foetus in Tirupattur
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Govt Schemes
fullParagraphs: Two persons were arrested by Vaniyambadi Taluk police in Tirupattur district on Saturday for conducting a sex determination test and attempting abortion of a foetus.
Police identified the arrested persons as K. Indrarani, 60, and S. Geetha, 45. They are residents of Chittoor district in Andhra Pradesh.
Initial inquiry revealed that V. Jagadeesan, 34, and his wife J. Pavithra, 28, both wage labourers, have two daughters.

As Pavithra became pregnant again, the couple reportedly got in touch with Indrarani and Geetha through agents to conduct a sex determination test, and found that the fetus was a girl. As the couple did not want a third girl child, they allegedly sought help from Indrarani and Geetha to abort the foetus.

Subsequently, the accused came to Jagadeesan’s house in Girisamudiram village on Saturday. Based on a tip-off, a team of health officials led by N. Kalu Sivalingam, District Health Officer (DHO) and S. Aravind, health officer, inspected the house and found medical equipment.
Police said, along with police personnel from Vaniyambadi Taluk, the team conducted an inquiry with the suspects, who confessed that they were roped in by the couple to abort the foetus.
Police said a case was registered under the Medical Termination of Pregnancy (MTP) Act, 1971. Later, two suspects were lodged at a sub-jail in Tirupattur town. Further probe is under way.

articles.title: IOC says crude Q2 price volatile as procurement swings between discounts and premiums
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Budget & Banking
fullParagraphs: Crude oil procurement remained volatile during the September quarter, with Indian Oil Corporation (IOC) sourcing supplies at discounts of up to $5 per barrel and premiums of as much as $12, Anuj Jain, Director (Finance), told investors during a post-results call on Saturday.

The Delhi-headquartered refiner’s net profit more than doubled year-on-year to ₹21,630 crore in the second quarter, supported by improved refining margins and a brief decline in benchmark crude oil prices.
Mr. Jain said LPG under-recoveries stood at ₹184 per cylinder in September before rising to ₹229 in October. These are projected to increase further to ₹309 in November and ₹370 in December.

Explaining the volatility in procurement costs, he said crude purchases during the quarter ranged from a discount of $5 per barrel to a premium of $12 against prevailing benchmark prices. In the first quarter, the range was from zero discount or premium to a premium of $18 per barrel.
Effective procurement prices depend on several factors, including whether supplies are contracted on a free-on-board (FOB) or delivered-at-place (DAP) basis, freight costs and the grade of crude.

Russian crude accounted for around 55% of IOC’s crude basket during the first half of the fiscal, followed by supplies from the Middle East, primarily Saudi Arabia and Dubai, at 24%. Africa, including Angola and Nigeria, contributed about 10%, while Brazil accounted for 7%. Supplies from the U.S. and Venezuela made up the remaining 2-5% and 3-4%, respectively.
Around 87% of the company’s crude procurement during the period came through spot sourcing. Mr. Jain said.
Responding to a question on whether spot purchases entailed higher costs, he said such sourcing did not necessarily mean paying a premium, as prices varied across region/geography.
“Now, within spot you have Russian crude. Sometimes, we are getting a high discount, sometimes we are paying a premium as well,” Mr. Jain said.

“In the few months, we have seen huge, discounted crude coming in from Iraq. So, the moment it is available, we are buying huge quantities from Iraq also. That used to be our staple diet before the [West Asia] crisis as well.”
He added that procurement economics were also influenced by effective negotiations, which played an important role in determining the final price.

articles.title: Towards recognising women farmers
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Budget & Banking
fullParagraphs: Picture a farmer. The image that comes to mind is of a man. But when one looks at who is actually farming, she is increasingly likely to be a woman. This perception-reality mismatch is caused by age-old practices of collecting data, designing policies and defining who a farmer is. It makes millions of women who work on farms, make agricultural decisions and contribute to production nearly invisible. That may, however, finally be beginning to change.

In July 2026, Maharashtra passed the Women Farmers’ Empowerment Bill, granting women independent recognition as farmers irrespective of land ownership, through a Woman Farmer Certificate. This is the first Indian State legislation to give enforceable legal form to the activity-based, land-delinked definition of ‘farmer’ that the National Policy for Farmers set out in 2007 but never operationalised. The Bill arrives nearly two decades after that policy, and 15 years after a comparable law was first proposed at the national level (a lapsed bill introduced in the Rajya Sabha in 2011). It is, in effect, the culmination of three decades of women farmers’ movements backed by civil society organisations.

articles.title: Petrol export duty cut to nil, diesel levy raised by ₹3 a litre
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Budget & Banking
fullParagraphs: The government on Saturday (October 31, 2026) slashed the export duty on petrol to nil while hiking the levy on export of diesel and aviation turbine fuel (ATF) by ₹3 per litre and 50 paise per litre respectively for the next 15-day period.
There was no change in the existing excise duty rates for petrol and diesel for domestic consumption.
Diesel exports would now draw a levy of ₹11.5 for every litre against ₹8.5 per litre it drew in the previous fortnight.
ATF would be subject to an export levy of ₹11 for every litre against ₹10.5 for every litre as mandated for the previous fortnight.
The revised levy on diesel assumes significance as India spiked its exports of the liquid vehicular fuel amid a global supply crunch, particularly in Europe.
According to data from real-time analytics provider Kpler, India’s diesel exports stood at 700 kilo barrels per day in October, the highest since September 2025.

Sumit Ritolia, Manager for Modelling and Refining at Kpler, in a social media post on Friday (October 30, 2026) further observed, “India’s diesel exports are expected to ease to 500-550 kbd in Nov–Dec as seasonal domestic demand peaks before recovering to 550–600 kbd in Q1 2027. Higher maintenance in Q2-27 will constrain export, with new capacity contributing meaningfully only later in 2027.”

The government has been conducting a fortnightly review of export levies since March 27, in the backdrop of the conflict in West Asia. These are done based on the average international benchmark prices of crude oil, petrol, diesel and ATF observed since the previous review.
This is to ensure the domestic availability of retail fuels by disincentivising exports.

articles.title: Disinvestment as key economic strategy
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Budget & Banking
fullParagraphs: S even months into 2026-27, the fiscal year has been shaped by global uncertainty, high energy prices and worries over a deficient monsoon. Against this backdrop, disinvestment and asset monetisation have helped in navigating a challenging fiscal year. While receipts were already on course to meet the budget target, the government’s approval of the sale of its share in the IDBI Bank on October 14 makes it likely that the target will be exceeded. For the industry and investors, the receipts are a signal of the government’s continued commitment to reforms and a larger role for the private sector. This year so far, the disinvestment trajectory has progressed well, even before the IDBI stake sale. According to DIPAM data, the Centre mobilised ₹62,124 crore in April-September 2026 through disinvestment and asset monetisation, of which ₹55,757 crore came from disinvestment. These collections had already reached 78% of the full-year budget target of ₹80,000 crore. With the IDBI proceeds, the collections are to head past the target.

This comes at a time when the government looks to diversify its revenue sources amid rising expenditure commitments. Net tax revenue rose by a modest 3.4% in April-August 2026 and non-tax revenue by 3.2%, while capital expenditure was up by over 18%. Overall, the fiscal deficit has already reached 42% of the budgeted levels which implies a tight balance between revenue shortfalls and spending risks.

articles.title: Coal India profit jumps 57% as higher offtake, prices weigh over costs
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Budget & Banking
fullParagraphs: Coal India’s net profit surged 57% year-on-year (YoY) to ₹6,547 crore in the second quarter, driven by higher offtake and improved price realisations that offset an increase in input costs.
The state-owned coal miner declared a second interim dividend of ₹10.25 per equity share.

Offtake during the quarter ended September increased 12% YoY to 186.34 million tonnes (MT), primarily driven by higher power demand. Average price realisation, covering fuel supply agreements, e-auctions, washed coal and other categories, rose 7% YoY to ₹2,346.21 per tonne.
The Kolkata-headquartered company’s overall production grew 4% YoY to 151.37 MT in the reported quarter, falling short of its target of 157.83 MT.
Revenue from the sale of products increased 21% YoY to ₹43,724 crore. Overall revenue also rose 21% to ₹44,179 crore.

The company’s cost of materials -- which primarily includes expenditure on explosives, oil and lubricants, heavy earth-moving machinery, spares and timber, among other items -- increased 20% YoY to ₹2,752 crore during the quarter.

articles.title: Deepavali sales expected to gain momentum in Coimbatore next week
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Budget & Banking
fullParagraphs: Shopping for the Deepavali festival in Coimbatore city this year is expected to pick up next week across sectors.
President of the Indian Chamber of Commerce and Industry, Coimbatore, C. Dorairaj, told The Hindu on Thursday (October 29) that several companies in Coimbatore will disburse bonuses next week.

With the festival coming in the first week of a month this year, people are likely to start purchases after getting the monthly salary and the festival bonus. So, the last 5-6 days preceding the festival is expected to see huge retail activity.
Be it textiles, FMCG, or household appliances, the retailers are expecting good sales this year.

All the products have seen a price hike, ranging between 10% and 30%, in the last few months, depending on the product. So, the retailers may see higher revenue though the volume of sales may remain the same as last year or slightly better in some sectors, he added.

In the case of textiles, while the large, multi brand retail outlets are already witnessing a pick up of sales, the smaller outlets are facing stiff competition from online sellers. Further, business at the small retail shops will go up in the last few days before the festival.

Though gold and silver prices saw a decline recently, jewellery retailers are yet to see business picking up. “We were hoping for better sales as the prices fell. But, consumers are waiting for further fall in prices,” said B. Sabarinath, president of the Coimbatore Jewellers Association.
The household appliances outlets are also expecting better sales only from next week.
In the case of sweets and savouries, most of the bulk buyers will purchase products for distribution just days before the festival, Mr. Dorairaj said.

articles.title: Rubio says U.S. not directly involved in Flavio Bolsonaro’s flight from Brazil
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Foreign Visits & UN/G20/BRICS
fullParagraphs: U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio said on Saturday (October 31, 2026) that Washington was not directly involved in Flavio Bolsonaro’s arrangements to leave Brazil after his election loss.

Mr. Bolsonaro, who lost his bid to be president in Sunday’s (October 25, 2026) run-off vote, arrived with his family in the U.S. on Wednesday (October 28, 2026) after a court ordered his passports be seized amid multiple investigations against him.

“He had previously held a visa, and the President made a decision to allow him to enter the country,” Mr. Rubio told a press conference in Atlanta, Georgia, where he hosted G20 Foreign Ministers for a two-day meeting.
But Mr. Rubio added that “the U.S. government was not involved directly” in arrangements Mr. Bolsonaro made to leave his country.

Following the vote, the 45-year-old bolted from Brazil via Argentina and Ecuador in a plane that some U.S. media, including The New York Times and The Wall Street Journa l, reported was chartered by Jason Miller, an adviser to U.S. President Donald Trump.
The plane that whisked the Mr. Bolsonaro family to the United States was paid for by an intermediary from a U.S. bank account, the head of the airline has told AFP .
The White House has not commented on the flight, but Mr. Trump has called the Brazilian election “disgraceful.”

A Brazilian diplomatic source, speaking on condition of anonymity, told AFP that Argentina’s diplomatic representative had been summoned for a “routine meeting” to “provide explanations” on the flight.
Argentina’s Foreign Minister later denied that Brazil had asked Buenos Aires to explain its role in the operation.
Since arriving in the U.S., Mr. Bolsonaro has claimed to be the true leader of Brazil and said that he left the country because he was a victim of “persecution.”
Flavio Bolsonaro’s father, former president Jair Bolsonaro, is serving a 27-year sentence under house arrest for plotting a coup after his 2022 re-election loss.

articles.title: Clashes break out between police and protesters in Paris
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Foreign Visits & UN/G20/BRICS
fullParagraphs: The French government estimated that 320,000 people protested nationwide on Saturday (October 31, 2026) in demonstrations focused on high living costs, fewer than in previous demonstrations.

Mass protests on October 17 drew more than 500,000 people around France, and demonstrations on October 24 drew 410,000, according to government estimates. Organisers’ turnout estimates are much higher.

The Interior Ministry told reporters that of the 320,000 protesting on Saturday (October 31, 2026), 70,000 people are estimated to have turned out for the main protest in Paris, which police moved outside the city centre to reduce the risk of unrest around government buildings and tourist sites after a last-minute court battle.

This is the third consecutive weekend of protests over living costs and education, deploying 70,000 police and gendarmes and rerouting the Paris march to the capital's edge as youth-led demonstrations spread across Europe.
Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez had warned of a “very high risk” of disorder, especially after dark on Halloween.

Paris police had banned union and “yellow vest” marches through the city centre, ordering demonstrations to follow a single route along the capital's outer boulevards, from Porte de Bagnolet to Porte de Charenton. Unions and student groups challenged the restrictions in court, but lost.
President Emmanuel Macron said on Monday (October 26, 2026) that marches would stay out of city centres to protect shops.
Police also barred entry to Place de la Republique and Les Halles, both hit by rioting and looting on October 17, from 11 p.m. to 6 a.m. on Saturday (October 31, 2026) and Sunday (November 1, 2026).

Unaccompanied minors face a separate 9 p.m. curfew around the Champs-Elysees. A Paris court on Wednesday (October 28, 2026) suspended an earlier curfew on minors as a serious and illegal infringement of freedom of movement.
The movement began with high school students protesting school conditions and broadened into anger over living costs.

Authorities counted about 550,000 protesters nationwide on October 17, when rioters looted hundreds of shops, and 410,000 last Saturday (October 31, 2026), when rallies were largely peaceful but police made more than 1,300 arrests.

In Germany, a youth initiative called “Gen Z regelt” — roughly “Gen Z's got this” — urged protests in some 30 cities “for education, health, climate protection and an affordable life,” and against any return of military conscription. Organisers said more than 140,000 people had signed up online.

articles.title: Pakistan PM orders fast-tracking of development projects in Gilgit-Baltistan
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Foreign Visits & UN/G20/BRICS
fullParagraphs: Pakistan Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif has directed officials to accelerate ongoing federal development projects in the controversial Gilgit-Baltistan region and ensure timely release of funds.

Mr. Sharif issued the directions while chairing a meeting in Islamabad on Friday (October 30, 2026) to review the progress of development projects in the region bordering China. Gilgit-Baltistan Chief Minister Amjad Hussain also attended the meeting.

The development assumes significance for India as Gilgit-Baltistan is illegally and forcibly occupied by Pakistan. The region is also a key component of the China-Pakistan Economic Corridor (CPEC), which passes through Pakistan-occupied Kashmir.
India has consistently opposed the CPEC projects passing through territories under Pakistan's illegal occupation, citing concerns over its sovereignty and territorial integrity.

According to state-run broadcaster Radio Pakistan , Mr. Sharif directed the authorities to remove all bottlenecks hindering development projects on a priority basis and ensure effective coordination among the relevant institutions to expedite implementation.

The meeting also reviewed progress on hydropower, infrastructure and solar energy projects in Gilgit-Baltistan. The Prime Minister directed the earliest possible completion of the 100-megawatt solar power project initiated by the federal government for the region.
The meeting also discussed the completion of the China-funded Naltar power project and the installation of digital infrastructure in the region.
The Prime Minister called for regular monitoring of development projects, particularly those related to the energy sector.

A report of a committee constituted in July on the Prime Minister's directives was also presented at the meeting. It reviewed the status of ongoing federal development projects, hurdles in their implementation and measures needed to ensure their timely completion.
Mr. Sharif is likely to visit Gilgit-Baltistan on November 1, the state-run broadcaster reported.

Gilgit-Baltistan, located in northern Pakistan, holds strategic importance because of its geographical proximity to China and its position along the route of the CPEC, a flagship infrastructure and connectivity initiative linking China's Xinjiang region with Pakistan's Gwadar port.
India maintains that the entire Union Territories of Jammu & Kashmir and Ladakh, including the so-called Gilgit-Baltistan, are integral and inalienable parts of the country.

articles.title: Beyond Cyclone Arnab: can India tackle the growing cost of natural disasters? | Insight India
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Updates, Tech & Climate Reports
fullParagraphs: Cyclone Arnab hit the coast of Andhra Pradesh this week. In preparation, authorities evacuated people, halted transportation services and alerted disaster response forces. This is just the first cyclone of the northeast monsoon season. As climate change threatens to bring increasingly intense cyclones and other natural disasters, will India’s current disaster management programme be able to handle the social and economic costs I?n this episode, Sonikka Loganathan speaks to Safi Ahsan Rizvi, former Adviser to the National Disaster Management Authority, about what goes into disaster management, the costs to the economy and vulnerable populations, and how India has improved its strategy since 1999.

articles.title: On umbrellas, springs, and superconductivity
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Updates, Tech & Climate Reports
fullParagraphs: Well after a few months of a hectic summer, rains are here. The campus is green and nature is once again abundant. With rains, however, has also come a usual game of hide and seek. Every time I take my umbrella out, the rain is nowhere to be seen. But when I forget it, I am greeted by sudden bouts of rain spoiling my ambition to reach my class dry and tidy.

Umbrellas, however, have something amazing about them. You press a button and it automatically opens up, stretches itself, and unfolds into a shade, growing much larger than it was. Like a magical genie.

articles.title: India’s first fusion power company takes key steps
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Updates, Tech & Climate Reports
fullParagraphs: If all goes to plan, India may see designs for the first privately built tokamak, a nuclear reactor that uses fusion to produce energy, firmed up in 2027.

Bengaluru-based startup Pranos Fusion has built PRAGYA, a small doughnut shaped tokamak, to test plasma control and superconducting magnets. This is a gateway to building PRANIK, a much larger tokomak that will have plasma heated up to millions of degrees — more than the interior of the Sun — necessary to fuse hydrogen atoms and create energy.

“By 2027, we expect to finalise the blueprint for PRANIK and be on our way to building a practical reactor that can produce energy. To be able to actually produce electricity from fusion is a further step away,” Shaurya Kaushal, co-founder and CEO of Pranos Fusion, said.

The company is currently incubated out of the Institute of Plasma Research, a body affiliated to the Department of Atomic Energy and the Jawaharlal Nehru Centre for Advanced Scientific Research (JNCASR), Bengaluru, an institute with the Department of Science and Technology.

Nuclear plants everywhere employ fission — a chain reaction involving uranium nuclei to produce heat that is used to generate electricity. Fusion, on the other hand, releases energy when light atomic nuclei merge, and usually involves joining two forms of hydrogen — deuterium and tritium — into helium and a fast neutron. However, this requires the fuel to be heated to around 100 million degrees Celsius, far hotter than any solid wall could withstand. In tokamaks, powerful magnets hold this superheated plasma away from the walls, keeping it hot enough for fusion to continue.
Pranos Fusion was one of the deeptech startups showcased at the Emerging Science Technology and Innovation Conclave held here last week.

“Electricity from a fusion reactor is still far away and would be expensive now, however the need for any source of energy is only going to grow,” Roshan George, co-founder and a Computer Science engineer from the Manipal Institute of Technology. “Fusion’s advantage is that while [it’s] nuclear power, it doesn’t need radioactive material like uranium. India already produces plenty of deuterium. Fusion reactions are also not chain reactions, and therefore the risk of a runaway reaction [like in a fission reactor] is almost absent,” Mr. George said.

The largest tokamak under construction is the International Thermonuclear Experimental Reactor in southern France, a collaboration between China, the European Union, India, Japan, Russia, South Korea, and the U.S. It is designed to produce about 10 times the heating power fed into its plasma. Bogged by delays, a 2024 revision moved the start of research operations to 2034 and full deuterium-tritium operation to 2039, adding about €5 billion to the cost. IPR manages India’s home-grown tokamak reactors, including ADITYA and the Steady State Tokamak (SST-1). It is also the nodal domestic agency to manage India’s contributions to International Thermonuclear Experimental Reactor.

The cost of a private tokamak depends on scale, Mr. Kaushal, who holds a Ph.D. from JNCASR, and a mechanical engineering degree from BITS Pilani, said. A compact research machine like PRAGYA is “a comparatively modest investment”, while one designed to reach net energy gain is far larger. Private fusion companies worldwide have raised over $13 billion, he said, and the leading net-gain programmes have each raised hundreds of millions of dollars or more.

Pranos Fusion says compact machines, HTS (high-temperature superconducting) magnets, and India’s manufacturing base can bring costs down substantially. It is backed by Ankur Capital, pi Ventures and Industrial47, and has raised $7.2 million. HTS electromagnets are wound from materials that carry electric current with no resistance when cooled below a critical temperature.

Britain’s JET tokamak produced a record 69 megajoules of fusion energy in 2023, though less than the heating power supplied. In December 2022, the U.S. National Ignition Facility, which uses lasers rather than magnets, achieved ignition, releasing more fusion energy than the laser light delivered to the fuel. This, however, does not count the electricity needed to run the lasers. Magnets made from high-temperature superconductors (HTS) have reached fields of around 20 tesla in tests, making smaller, stronger-field machines feasible.

In an email, Mr. Kaushal said the company is structured in a way its technology generates value before a power plant exists. It has two platforms — JENGA, simulation, design and control software that works as a digital twin of the machine, and MAGGA, its HTS magnet programme.

articles.title: NASA telescope on verge of plunging back to Earth after failed rescue mission
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Updates, Tech & Climate Reports
fullParagraphs: An ageing NASA telescope is barely clinging to space after a failed rescue effort left it tottering lower and lower.
The U.S. Space Force predicts the Swift Observatory will come crashing down on or around Friday (October 30, 2026).

Most of the 1 ½-ton telescope is expected to burn up in the atmosphere. But a handful of pieces made of denser-than-lead tungsten and some mirror parts could survive reentry, according to NASA's Brad Cenko, the mission's chief scientist.

Any surviving wreckage will most likely plunge into the ocean. But swaths of Africa, Australia, India, Southeast Asia, and Central and South America are within the reentry zone. The Space Force is tracking the telescope's dwindling path.

Its cosmic cremation has the Swift team mourning, yet full of gratitude for the observations the telescope made during its 22 years in orbit. Swift blasted off on November 20, 2004, to search for some of the biggest explosions in the universe — gamma ray bursts and supernovas.

“We've known this day would come since before Swift was launched. At least in low-Earth orbit, what goes up must come down. And that end is catastrophic,” said Pennsylvania State University's John Nousek, an astronomer who led the control team.

Intense solar activity over the past few years dragged Swift down faster than usual. NASA hired Katalyst Space a year ago to mount a rush rescue. But the company's three-armed robot named Link ran into trouble after launching in July and got no closer than 7 miles to 9 miles (12 kilometres to 15 kilometres) to the telescope. Link plunged back to Earth in September.

Swift resumed observations once the rescue attempt was called off, discovering even more gamma ray bursts and other ultrahigh-energy events. But by late October, the telescope was too low to remain steady for observations, and its systems were shut down.

Its final tally — more than 2,000 gamma ray bursts and 1,400 exploding stars, not to mention a slew of comets, asteroids, and star-shredding black holes. The telescope's superpower was its ability to swivel swiftly — thus its name — toward erupting celestial events.

NASA considered Swift a first responder for the Hubble and Webb space telescopes and others that would follow its alerts and provide deeper investigations. Scientists are still figuring out how to fill the gap.

“Our fervent hope is that the lessons learned by the successes of Swift can be applied to new generations of space missions to accelerate our discoveries about the universe,” Mr. Nousek said in an email.

articles.title: Beyond gullibility: On digital arrest scams
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: Chief Justice of India Surya Kant’s exasperation, during the Supreme Court’s hearing on October 29 on the “digital arrest” scams, that people still fall for such scams despite abundant warnings and orders from the Court is understandable. About ₹800 crore has been lost to these scams this year even after recoveries, a hefty sum from the savings of individual victims. But this is not merely about gullibility. Scammers posing as CBI or police officers succeed because their victims, older citizens in particular, defer to or fear law enforcement. When Indian police are widely seen as high-handed towards ordinary citizens and as serving only the powerful, the threat of an “arrest” over a video call cannot be that implausible for many. That said, the Court’s pressing of the Reserve Bank of India to finalise its KYC Amendment Directions, 2026, which require banks to flag suspected mule accounts and put temporary debit holds on them, is welcome. CBI investigations have shown that mule accounts are central to scammers laundering their proceeds after duping victims and that bank staff have, in some cases, helped open them. With the availability of complete transaction histories and AI tools, banks can now spot anomalous transactions faster. The Attorney-General’s assurance that the directions will be in force by December 31 is also welcome. The Court’s insistence that banks compensate victims addresses an issue with the RBI’s zero-liability provisions. Its 2017 circular covers only unauthorised transactions, leaving victims who were coerced into making transfers without any recourse.

Yet, full compensation for the victims whenever banks are found wanting in due diligence must be implemented with care as this might force banks to flag far more than the actual mule accounts. Already the RBI directions cast a wide net. Any transaction of ₹1,000 or more that is ‘unusual’ for an account holder’s declared profile, or linked to a reported account, can be held for up to 60 days, and longer if directed by the police. In cases where small traders and Jan Dhan account holders have unknowingly received transfers from mule accounts, freezing their accounts for two months or more is a disproportionate penalty. Also, the Court’s suggestion that unusual transactions must be automatically reported to the police and physically verified raises privacy concerns. These measures must ensure that genuine account holders are not penalised for bank failures. Many of these scams are run from compounds using trafficked Indians in conflict-ridden parts of Myanmar and in Cambodia and Laos where they have thrived due to some degree of official patronage. India must use its clout to pressure these regimes.

articles.title: Suboptimal outcomes: On social security boards for unorganised, gig, platform workers
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: One year after the implementation of the Code on Social Security , the Union Labour Ministry has constituted the National Social Security Boards for Unorganised Workers and Gig and Platform Workers. The constitution of the boards, though delayed, is a welcome step. However, the highly centralised nature of this mechanism may hinder its optimal outcomes. By design, the Union Government controls both the Boards: they will be chaired by Union Minister for Labour Mansukh Mandaviya. The Board for Unorganised Sector Workers will have 40 members, nominated by the Union Government. They include seven members representing unorganised sector workers and seven members representing employers of the unorganised sector. Similarly, the Board for the welfare of gig and platform workers will have 22 members with five representatives each from the aggregators and the workers. But they have no significant representation of Central Trade Unions from the Opposition side or from the State Governments ruled by the Opposition. Labour is in the Concurrent List of the Constitution and both the States and the Union must work together to improve the living standards of workers.

The International Labour Organization defines social security as the ‘protection that a society provides to individuals and households to ensure access to health care and to guarantee income security, particularly in cases of old age, unemployment, sickness, invalidity, work injury, maternity or loss of a breadwinner’. The Union Government claims that the country’s social security coverage has increased from 19% in 2015 to 64.3% in 2025, which is around 94 crore citizens. However, it is apparent that the unorganised and gig and platform workers, who make up more than 92% of the country’s total workforce, are far from enjoying any social security under this definition. Almost two decades ago, the National Commission for Enterprises in the Unorganised Sector, headed by economist Arjun Sengupta, recommended a slew of measures to improve the social security of workers in the informal sector. The issues raised by the panel still remain unaddressed. A report prepared by Justice V. Gopala Gowda for the Keralam Government in March this year flagged certain anti-federal and anti-worker characteristics in the Social Security Code and suggested amendments. The Union Government should take the trade unions and the State Governments on board while creating new systems and mechanisms to address the social security concerns of the vast majority of workers.

articles.title: Open to investigation: On the challenge to the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: The Digital News Publishers Association’s (DNPA) challenge to the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 , and its Rules , has drawn attention to concerns that a law to safeguard informational privacy risks creating a serious chilling effect on the media. The absence of a specific exemption for journalistic activity could subject reporters investigating official misconduct or corruption to the obligations of a “data fiduciary”, requiring them to notify and seek consent from the very individuals they are investigating. Such onerous requirements could affect investigations undertaken in the public interest. The implications extend to routine newsgathering too, where personal information is integral to reporting. The omission is particularly consequential because the drafts in 2018, 2019 and 2021 carried a journalistic exemption. The Act already provides exemptions for certain forms of data processing, including for research and statistical purposes, making the denial of similar protection to journalists difficult to justify. Non-compliance can attract penalties of up to ₹250 crore, posing an existential threat to smaller and independent newsrooms. The DNPA petition also challenges Section 44(3), which amended the RTI Act, 2005, removing the earlier public-interest qualification concerning disclosure of personal information. The protection of personal information must not be absolute; an overriding public interest must remain a legitimate ground for disclosure, particularly when the information is held by public authorities. Investigations into corruption often rely on asset disclosures and tender documents containing personal data. Restricting access to these records risks reducing journalism to merely reproducing government releases.

The Supreme Court, while issuing notice on the petition, rightly emphasised the need to balance press freedom with the right to privacy. Although journalists in India enjoy no specific statutory protection for their work, freedom of the press is constitutionally protected under Article 19(1)(a). The Court has also shielded newspapers from arbitrary state restrictions. However, growing mistrust of legacy media and the rise of independent content creators have made it difficult to determine who receives such protection. The Centre has also flagged this concern. articles.title: Deemed ineligible: On the Supreme Court and SIR
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: At Wednesday’s hearing of a petition on the Delhi SIR in the Supreme Court, Justice Joymalya Bagchi asked questions that cut to the heart of the Election Commission of India (ECI)’s SIR of electoral rolls . If an existing voter was “lax, inert or did not respond” to enumeration forms, was that a ground for the ECI to “forfeit his or her right to vote forever”? The Bench headed by the Chief Justice of India Surya Kant said that the ECI was in “error” to force such voters, struck off for not returning enumeration forms, to reapply on Form 6 as if they were new voters. It asked why voters who had shifted residences could not just disclose details and why deleted voters could not fill enumeration forms belatedly. This is the central design flaw of the SIR as it shifts the burden of enrolment from the state to the elector, including those who have voted before, and treats a mere change of address as ground for deletion. The share of draft deletions recorded as “shifted” or “absent” rose from 55% in Bihar to 72% in States/Union Territories in Phase 3. In Karnataka, about 84 lakh electors were deleted, marked as “shifted” or “absent” during enumeration. But only a net of 8.2 lakh, including new electors, were added during the claims phase, with the final roll being 64.5 lakh short of the projected adult population. Requiring moved voters to re-register as fresh applicants defeats the ECI’s historic mandate of widening the franchise, which was inherent in the 2002-03 intensive revision, where enumerators enrolled shifted voters at their new homes and the Chief Electoral Officer reconciled the old entries.

Justice Bagchi also mentioned that the Bihar judgment was not a “binding precedent” and that the legality of “logical discrepancy” checks, allowed only as an “interim arrangement” in West Bengal, had not been finally adjudicated. No statute or rule provides for judging a voter’s eligibility on the basis of family size or the age gap between voters and parents, which were two of the ECI’s ludicrous and algorithm-driven “logical discrepancy” checks. In West Bengal these checks resulted in massive disenfranchisement and The Hindu’s analysis found that in Delhi, Muslims were disproportionately flagged. But the Court should not merely issue managerial fixes such as extended deadlines or displaying printed lists in blocks, as it has in the past. The final SIR rolls are erroneous as deletions flowed from a flawed design rather than just lapses by the ECI. The dead and duplicate entries that the SIR identified should be removed and newly eligible electors added. Voters wrongly removed from draft rolls must be included again. The larger questions over the Commission’s SIR conduct and how its members are appointed must also be settled.

articles.title: Clinging on: On Netanyahu and the Israel elections
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: Benjamin Netanyahu was at the centre of Israel’s October 27 elections. For Israel’s longest-serving Prime Minister, who oversaw a genocidal war in Gaza following Hamas’s October 7 attack , the election was the biggest test of his political career. For the Opposition, which promised to hold him accountable for the failures of October 7 and end the country’s “forever wars”, the election offered an opportunity to oust him from power. The results, however, sent a mixed message. With 85.6% of the votes counted, Mr. Netanyahu’s right-religious coalition has lost its majority but is still the largest bloc . His Likud party is projected to win 26 seats, while its main rival Yashar, led by former military chief Gadi Eisenkot, is expected to secure 21. Otzma Yehudit and Religious Zionism, the far-right extremist parties in Mr. Netanyahu’s coalition, demonstrated their continued strength, winning 13 seats between them. The dark horse, however, could be the Arab parties — the Joint List is projected to win 12 seats while the United Arab List (Ra’am) could secure seven seats. With neither bloc commanding a majority, the Arab parties could propel the opposition coalition to power. But the big question is whether the anti-Netanyahu coalition is ready to join hands with the Arab parties, which have historically been kept on the margins of Israel’ s power politics.

Mr. Netanyahu’s central promise has been that only he can guarantee Israel’s security. Yet, the October 7 attack took place on his watch and he has refused to take responsibility for the failures that led to it. A wanted man by the International Criminal Court, he has repeated, before and after October 7, that a Palestine state would not be formed while he is in power. His war on Gaza has killed over 70,000 Palestinians, including 20,000 children, and displaced the region’s population. Israel’s brutal occupation machinery has also expanded and tightened its control of the West Bank, while settler terrorists have unleashed violence on Palestinian households. His war on Iran has been a disaster, with global economic consequences. Mr. Netanyahu has sought to portray his wars as bold, necessary moves to protect Israel, while exploiting Israelis’ security concerns for political gain. He may not be voted out immediately, but his failure to secure a majority and the decline in his party’s popularity are significant. The Opposition should take its cue from the results and form a broad coalition with the Arab parties. It should restore accountability in governance, revisit his unchecked militarism and rebuild ties with the world. If Mr. Netanyahu continues to cling to power, it would be bad news for Israel and the region.

articles.title: Hunker down: On Cyclone Arnab, its landfall
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: Cyclone Arnab, the first named storm of the North Indian Ocean cyclone season this year, intensified rapidly before making landfall as a ‘very severe cyclonic storm’ on October 28. This particular rapidity is a challenge for forecasters and some models did fail to anticipate how strong Arnab would become. It also moved faster than expected towards the coast, before stalling for a time and beginning the landfall process several hours before the India Meteorological Department (IMD) had predicted it would, in the middle of the night, leaving many district authorities with a potentially narrower window to evacuate high-risk settlements. With core wind speeds of 125-135 kilometres per hour, it delivered more than 100 mm of rain over parts of Anakapalli, Visakhapatnam, Kalingapatnam, Kakinada and Machilipatnam, in Andhra Pradesh. But even though it has completed landfall, southern Odisha likely faces a greater threat only hence. Early reports claimed no loss of life in Andhra Pradesh or Odisha, which has been attributed to the disaster management operations in both States; the Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister, N. Chandrababu Naidu, said there were five deaths in Andhra Pradesh . Regrettably, the suspension of transport services, including road connectivity and flights, closure of schools and offices, and power cuts to minimise risks posed by loose wires remains an essential part of saving lives, entailing other social and economic disruptions that the States must account for, and address, in their post-storm assessments.

Odisha may have to brace for rainfall and waters due to moisture in the storm’s outer circulation, which will arrive over land that has recovered in patches from the fourth wettest monsoon in the State’s history. Extreme rainfall after repeated flooding may face soil that has not drained fully, raising the risk of more flooding following even lower levels of rainfall, and slope failures in hilly terrain. Farmers in Ganjam and Puri have already voiced worries about the risk of prolonged inundation destroying paddy crops, compounding the already considerable financial consequences of the southwest monsoon; Ganjam alone had lost 33% of crops by October. In Sundargarh, however, farmers hope that Arnab will relieve moisture stress in standing crops after a dry month. The IMD has already issued alerts in the Ganjam, Gajapati, Rayagada, Koraput, Malkangiri, Nabarangpur, and Kalahandi districts, before the rainbelt extends further north. The relatively low figure of deaths will be a testament to proactive governance. However, it is past time that States adopted a zero-disruption approach, especially since property and infrastructure were damaged, and the risk of people being pushed into poverty over lost possessions and livelihoods persists.

articles.title: Devotees worried over conduct of Kandasashti festival at Kandakottam temple
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Govt Schemes
fullParagraphs: Devotees of the Sri Muthukumaraswamy Temple, popularly known as Kandhakottam in Rattan Bazaar in Park Town, are worried about the conduct of the Kandasashthi festival this year.

"Usually, tickets for the Laksharcharnai during the annual festival are sold just after Vijayadasami. Till date, the administration has not started selling tickets. Every year around 35,000 tickets each priced at ₹300 are sold to devotees who want to participate in the archanai that is slated to start on November 10. There is no sign of the conduct of the festival so far," said A. B. Srinivasan, a 65-year-old devotee.

Saravanan, another devotee, said that this year would be the 99 th consecutive year of the Kandasashthi festival during which grand concerts would be held. "Participants of the archanai would be given prasadam including a bucket. Tenders for procuring various items such as pandals, coconuts, bags, and flowers are yet to be called for. We hear that the executive officer has gone on leave and another person has taken charge," he said.

The over 500-year-old shrine, is a scheme temple, meaning it belongs to a particular community - in this case, the Berri Chettis. A five-member team was chosen from the community as trustees last year and they have also been in charge of the daily running of the temple.

Sendilvellan, one of the trustees, said that the executive officer had taken away cheque signatory powers from the trustees and the trustees were unable to pay salaries even. "He has gone to the bank and taken signatory powers without informing us. We seem to have absolutely no powers in the day-to-day running of the temple. The court had directed the Hindu Religious and Charitable Endowments department to interfere only if there was any problem relating to the conduct of the temple. From last year, we have been managing the temple without any problems," he said.

Another trustee said that with just a few days left for the festival they have been running from pillar to post trying to get the powers back and conduct it. Sources in the HR&CE Department said they will look into the matter.

articles.title: Rajasthan IPS officer removed after ACB probe ordered against IAS husband
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Govt Schemes
fullParagraphs: The Rajasthan government on Saturday placed an Indian Police Service (IPS) officer, Prashakha Mathur, on awaiting posting order (APO) after an investigation by the Anti-Corruption Bureau (ACB) was approved against her husband and senior Indian Administrative Service (IAS) officer Shikhar Agrawal.

Mr. Agrawal, who was also sent on APO earlier this week, is facing charges along with his family members of purchasing 40 villas in luxury resorts operated by a private firm in Udaipur and Alwar districts by allegedly abusing his position and influence and extending “undue benefits” to the firm.

While Mr. Agrawal was serving as the Additional Chief Secretary (Industries) and additionally held charge of four public sector corporations, his wife Ms. Mathur, a 1995-batch IPS officer, was posted as Additional Director General in charge of Planning, Modernisation and Welfare.

The ACB has alleged that Mr. Agrawal gave benefits such as relaxations in resort construction conditions, approvals without verification of certificates and special concessional packages to the firm. The alleged purchases of villas were made in the names of Mr. Agrawal and Ms. Mathur, their two sons, and Mr. Agrawal’s parents-in-law.

The ACB has registered a Preliminary Enquiry (PE) and launched an investigation into the allegations of abuse of official position, conflict of interest, and extending undue benefits to the firm in question.

ACB Director General Govind Gupta said the properties were allegedly purchased at prices substantially below their market value. The ACB’s probe will examine whether the alleged benefits caused substantial financial losses to the State government and whether Mr. Agrawal and his family members acquired assets disproportionate to their known sources of income.

Mr. Agrawal was appointed Additional Chief Secretary in the Chief Minister’s Office in February 2024, shortly after Bhajan Lal Sharma took oath as the CM, and served in that position till November 2025. Former CM Ashok Gehlot has demanded investigation by Central agencies into the matter, describing it as the “biggest scandal” under the Bharatiya Janata Party government.

articles.title: At CEC’s ‘public impeachment’, voters question deletion of names from rolls
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Govt Schemes
fullParagraphs: The Indian National Developmental, Inclusive Alliance’s symbolic “public impeachment” of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar on Saturday (October 31, 2026) featured accounts from voters who alleged that their names had been deleted from electoral rolls during the special intensive revision (SIR) exercise.
Among them was Anita Jaiswal, who moved from Kolkata to Delhi. She said she had voted in every election between 2012 and 2025 but was now being asked to establish her citizenship.
ALSO WATCH Watch: INDIA bloc leaders present united front against CEC Gyanesh Kumar, holds mock impeachment

“I am a single mother. They told me to get an Aadhaar card, saying it would prove that I am a citizen. Who gave you the right to remove my voter ID? My daughter gets a scholarship, has a bank account and an Aadhaar card, and now you are deleting our names. Who gave you the right?” she asked, adding, “Prove which country I am from.”

Iftikar Ahmed, another voter from Kolkata, said he had voted in the same Chowrangee constituency for 20 years but received a notice during the SIR hearing seeking documents because of a mapping discrepancy. His father, too, had been voting from the same address for two decades, he said. “Our names have been removed in a planned manner,” he alleged.

Nikhil Dey, founder of Mazdoor Kisan Shakti Sangathan, who has been working with affected voters, introduced Kanta Prasad, who had been declared dead in the exercise. “He spoke very convincingly for a corpse! The deprivation of the right to vote is a crime against the Constitution and a blot on our democracy. There must be accountability,” Congress MP Shashi Tharoor said in a post on X.
ALSO WATCH Rahul Gandhi: Deletion of 1 in 7 voters makes 2024 election ‘illegitimate’ | INDIA bloc

RTI activist Anjali Bharadwaj said that in response to an application seeking copies of files recording the decision-making process behind the SIR, the Election Commission of India (ECI) had replied that no such file existed.
“T.C. Kom, who is a Principal Secretary, said the ECI had not taken any decision to conduct an SIR,” Ms. Bharadwaj claimed.
Swaraj Abhiyan chief Yogendra Yadav described Mr. Kumar as the “Mukhya Chunav Abhiyukt (Chief Election Culprit)” rather than the “Mukhya Chunav Ayukt (Chief Election Commissioner)”.

All India Students’ Association (AISA) national president Neha Bora alleged that the SIR was a deliberate attempt to disenfranchise young voters and undermine democracy. Questioning the functioning of electoral registration officers (EROs), she said their statutory authority was being overridden through the use of software to exclude eligible voters. “You have abused your public office and favoured one political party,” she alleged.

The programme was held in the garden of Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge’s residence in New Delhi. Former Lok Sabha Speaker Meira Kumar presided over the proceedings, while Mr. Kharge moved the motion.

articles.title: Two persons held for possession of country-made guns, explosives
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Govt Schemes
fullParagraphs: Two persons, including a farmer, were arrested for possession of two country made guns and crude bombs near Pallikonda and Pernambut towns in Vellore on Saturday.
Forest officials identified the arrested persons as U. Chandru, 21, a tribal from Irular community, and G. Srinivasan, 39, a farmer.

Initial inquiry revealed that Srinivasan has been cultivating paddy and groundnuts on his two acre farmland. Forest officials said that, based on a tip-off, a special team conducted searches at his house and farmland, and found country made guns, explosives, nets, torchlights, and batteries.
Forest officials said that Srinivasan procured guns from his contacts in Kerala. He used pellets to hunt monkeys, rabbits, and spotted deer in forests surrounding Jawadhu Hills.

In a separate incident, forest officials arrested Chandru, who was allegedly loitering with a country-made gun in the area. The team nabbed him during a regular patrol and seized the country-made gun, pellets, and explosives.
Forest officials said both arrested persons were lodged at Central Prison in Vellore. Further probe is under way.

articles.title: New bridge to be opened near Sholinghur to replace British-era structure
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Govt Schemes
fullParagraphs: A new ₹3.85 crore high-level bridge across the Rendadi Water Supply Channel near Ponnai River, at Sekkadikuppam village near Sholinghur town in Ranipet will be opened for public use by December this year.

Officials of the District Rural Development Agency (DRDA), which executes the work, said that the new facility was a long-standing demand of at least eight surrounding farming villages across the water channel. The new bridge will replace the British-era causeway, which was damaged during 2021 floods in the water channel, fed by Ponnai river.

The new bridge will provide easy access to villagers in Ranipet and Thiruvallur districts. “The new bridge will help farmers to transport farm products to common markets in surrounding big towns. Buses will also be operated to reach remote villages,” S. Kannan, Assistant Engineer (AE), DRDA (Sholinghur), told The Hindu.

On Saturday, Collector N. Priya Ravichandran inspected the under-construction bridge in the presence of S. Selvarani, Project Director (PD), DRDA (Ranipet), and Prabhakaran, Executive Engineer (EE), DRDA (Ranipet). “During monsoon, residents could not cross the water channel due to chest-deep water. The new bridge will be a lifeline for residents as ambulances and government buses can reach remote villages in the region,” said T. Perumal, a farmer.

DRDA officials said that the new bridge will replace the dilapidated causeway, which was demolished for the work, to connect surrounding villages with towns like Sholinghur, Arakkonam, Tiruvallur, and Tiruttani.

Funded under the State Special Assistance Scheme for 2025-26, the new bridge will be 38 metres long and 7.5 metres wide. It can discharge around 30,000 cusecs of water per second. The new facility has been built at least three metres above the water channel to prevent inundation during floods.

The new bridge will have tiled footpaths, LED lights, inlets to discharge rainwater into the river, reflectors, signboards and hand railings. Approach roads will also be laid to connect surrounding villages with the new facility.

For residents, the new bridges will end a detour of at least eight kms to reach the nearest towns in Ranipet and Thiruvallur districts. It will provide easy access to basic facilities like government schools, health centres, banks, ATMs, agricultural office, cooperative society and taluk office, residents said.

articles.title: Two arrested for attempting to determine sex of foetus in Tirupattur
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Govt Schemes
fullParagraphs: Two persons were arrested by Vaniyambadi Taluk police in Tirupattur district on Saturday for conducting a sex determination test and attempting abortion of a foetus.
Police identified the arrested persons as K. Indrarani, 60, and S. Geetha, 45. They are residents of Chittoor district in Andhra Pradesh.
Initial inquiry revealed that V. Jagadeesan, 34, and his wife J. Pavithra, 28, both wage labourers, have two daughters.

As Pavithra became pregnant again, the couple reportedly got in touch with Indrarani and Geetha through agents to conduct a sex determination test, and found that the fetus was a girl. As the couple did not want a third girl child, they allegedly sought help from Indrarani and Geetha to abort the foetus.

Subsequently, the accused came to Jagadeesan’s house in Girisamudiram village on Saturday. Based on a tip-off, a team of health officials led by N. Kalu Sivalingam, District Health Officer (DHO) and S. Aravind, health officer, inspected the house and found medical equipment.
Police said, along with police personnel from Vaniyambadi Taluk, the team conducted an inquiry with the suspects, who confessed that they were roped in by the couple to abort the foetus.
Police said a case was registered under the Medical Termination of Pregnancy (MTP) Act, 1971. Later, two suspects were lodged at a sub-jail in Tirupattur town. Further probe is under way.

articles.title: IOC says crude Q2 price volatile as procurement swings between discounts and premiums
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Budget & Banking
fullParagraphs: Crude oil procurement remained volatile during the September quarter, with Indian Oil Corporation (IOC) sourcing supplies at discounts of up to $5 per barrel and premiums of as much as $12, Anuj Jain, Director (Finance), told investors during a post-results call on Saturday.

The Delhi-headquartered refiner’s net profit more than doubled year-on-year to ₹21,630 crore in the second quarter, supported by improved refining margins and a brief decline in benchmark crude oil prices.
Mr. Jain said LPG under-recoveries stood at ₹184 per cylinder in September before rising to ₹229 in October. These are projected to increase further to ₹309 in November and ₹370 in December.

Explaining the volatility in procurement costs, he said crude purchases during the quarter ranged from a discount of $5 per barrel to a premium of $12 against prevailing benchmark prices. In the first quarter, the range was from zero discount or premium to a premium of $18 per barrel.
Effective procurement prices depend on several factors, including whether supplies are contracted on a free-on-board (FOB) or delivered-at-place (DAP) basis, freight costs and the grade of crude.

Russian crude accounted for around 55% of IOC’s crude basket during the first half of the fiscal, followed by supplies from the Middle East, primarily Saudi Arabia and Dubai, at 24%. Africa, including Angola and Nigeria, contributed about 10%, while Brazil accounted for 7%. Supplies from the U.S. and Venezuela made up the remaining 2-5% and 3-4%, respectively.
Around 87% of the company’s crude procurement during the period came through spot sourcing. Mr. Jain said.
Responding to a question on whether spot purchases entailed higher costs, he said such sourcing did not necessarily mean paying a premium, as prices varied across region/geography.
“Now, within spot you have Russian crude. Sometimes, we are getting a high discount, sometimes we are paying a premium as well,” Mr. Jain said.

“In the few months, we have seen huge, discounted crude coming in from Iraq. So, the moment it is available, we are buying huge quantities from Iraq also. That used to be our staple diet before the [West Asia] crisis as well.”
He added that procurement economics were also influenced by effective negotiations, which played an important role in determining the final price.

articles.title: Towards recognising women farmers
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Budget & Banking
fullParagraphs: Picture a farmer. The image that comes to mind is of a man. But when one looks at who is actually farming, she is increasingly likely to be a woman. This perception-reality mismatch is caused by age-old practices of collecting data, designing policies and defining who a farmer is. It makes millions of women who work on farms, make agricultural decisions and contribute to production nearly invisible. That may, however, finally be beginning to change.

In July 2026, Maharashtra passed the Women Farmers’ Empowerment Bill, granting women independent recognition as farmers irrespective of land ownership, through a Woman Farmer Certificate. This is the first Indian State legislation to give enforceable legal form to the activity-based, land-delinked definition of ‘farmer’ that the National Policy for Farmers set out in 2007 but never operationalised. The Bill arrives nearly two decades after that policy, and 15 years after a comparable law was first proposed at the national level (a lapsed bill introduced in the Rajya Sabha in 2011). It is, in effect, the culmination of three decades of women farmers’ movements backed by civil society organisations.

articles.title: Petrol export duty cut to nil, diesel levy raised by ₹3 a litre
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Budget & Banking
fullParagraphs: The government on Saturday (October 31, 2026) slashed the export duty on petrol to nil while hiking the levy on export of diesel and aviation turbine fuel (ATF) by ₹3 per litre and 50 paise per litre respectively for the next 15-day period.
There was no change in the existing excise duty rates for petrol and diesel for domestic consumption.
Diesel exports would now draw a levy of ₹11.5 for every litre against ₹8.5 per litre it drew in the previous fortnight.
ATF would be subject to an export levy of ₹11 for every litre against ₹10.5 for every litre as mandated for the previous fortnight.
The revised levy on diesel assumes significance as India spiked its exports of the liquid vehicular fuel amid a global supply crunch, particularly in Europe.
According to data from real-time analytics provider Kpler, India’s diesel exports stood at 700 kilo barrels per day in October, the highest since September 2025.

Sumit Ritolia, Manager for Modelling and Refining at Kpler, in a social media post on Friday (October 30, 2026) further observed, “India’s diesel exports are expected to ease to 500-550 kbd in Nov–Dec as seasonal domestic demand peaks before recovering to 550–600 kbd in Q1 2027. Higher maintenance in Q2-27 will constrain export, with new capacity contributing meaningfully only later in 2027.”

The government has been conducting a fortnightly review of export levies since March 27, in the backdrop of the conflict in West Asia. These are done based on the average international benchmark prices of crude oil, petrol, diesel and ATF observed since the previous review.
This is to ensure the domestic availability of retail fuels by disincentivising exports.

articles.title: Disinvestment as key economic strategy
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Budget & Banking
fullParagraphs: S even months into 2026-27, the fiscal year has been shaped by global uncertainty, high energy prices and worries over a deficient monsoon. Against this backdrop, disinvestment and asset monetisation have helped in navigating a challenging fiscal year. While receipts were already on course to meet the budget target, the government’s approval of the sale of its share in the IDBI Bank on October 14 makes it likely that the target will be exceeded. For the industry and investors, the receipts are a signal of the government’s continued commitment to reforms and a larger role for the private sector. This year so far, the disinvestment trajectory has progressed well, even before the IDBI stake sale. According to DIPAM data, the Centre mobilised ₹62,124 crore in April-September 2026 through disinvestment and asset monetisation, of which ₹55,757 crore came from disinvestment. These collections had already reached 78% of the full-year budget target of ₹80,000 crore. With the IDBI proceeds, the collections are to head past the target.

This comes at a time when the government looks to diversify its revenue sources amid rising expenditure commitments. Net tax revenue rose by a modest 3.4% in April-August 2026 and non-tax revenue by 3.2%, while capital expenditure was up by over 18%. Overall, the fiscal deficit has already reached 42% of the budgeted levels which implies a tight balance between revenue shortfalls and spending risks.

The Kolkata-headquartered company’s overall production grew 4% YoY to 151.37 MT in the reported quarter, falling short of its target of 157.83 MT.
Revenue from the sale of products increased 21% YoY to ₹43,724 crore. Overall revenue also rose 21% to ₹44,179 crore.

The company’s cost of materials -- which primarily includes expenditure on explosives, oil and lubricants, heavy earth-moving machinery, spares and timber, among other items -- increased 20% YoY to ₹2,752 crore during the quarter.
